text:
Maria: quick proposal — introduce a short "grace window" routing policy when v2 capacity is saturated so we can avoid immediate downgrade to v1 for short spikes. idea: 30s-2m window where requests stay queued for v2 before falling back.

Ashwin: curious about telemetry here — we need a signal to detect 'short spike' vs sustained outage. what metric do we base it on? p50 queue time? slot contention?

Maria: good q. proposal uses two signals: v2 pending queue length (threshold) + sustained dequeue failure rate for >5s. short spike = queue crosses threshold but dequeue succeeds within window. sustained outage = failure persists past window.

Ryan: ok but quota/cost impact — if we keep requests queued for 2m they might blow through user rate limits or increase token billing unexpectedly. we need per-tenant caps on queued tokens and a hard timeout.

Sophia: UX thought: Console should show a small badge per route: "fallback window active (45s)" with ability to override per-tenant. Also expose metric: "requests held" and "avg held time".

Zara: agree with both. also need deprecations team buy-in — how will this interact with v1->v2 rollout flags? if we hold for v2 we might change perceived rollout behavior.

Maria: rollout flags: default behavior opt-in via console flag for first rollout. we start with 30s global window, then increase to 60s if telemetry shows spike patterns. we can A/B test per-tenant.

Ashwin: for detection, I'd implement a short-timeseries detector: when queue_len > Q_thresh and successful dequeue rate in last 10s > 0 then mark as spike. Pseudocode: 

```
if queue_len > Q_thresh:
  if success_rate_10s > 0:
    enter GRACE state for window_s
  else:
    fallback immediately
```

We should log a single event with reason codes: GRACE_ENTER, GRACE_EXIT_SUCCESS, GRACE_EXIT_FALLBACK.

Ryan: that helps. also need to cap queued token sum per API token: max_queued_tokens = min(tenant_quota_tokens * 0.2, 50k). if exceeded, bypass grace and fallback immediately.

Sophia: console UI: show toggle and per-tenant slider for max window and max queued tokens. default to managed mode but allow manual override for enterprise customers. need a small help tooltip describing cost risks.

Maria: telemetry requirements: we need these metrics emitted as traces and metrics: route.queue_len, route.queued_tokens, route.grace_state, route.grace_duration, route.fallback_reason. also increment a counter per tenant: grace_succeeded, grace_failed.

Zara: can we add an alerting rule for "grace_fail_rate > 1% over 5m" so SRE gets pinged if lots of forced fallbacks?

Ashwin: yes. we should also tag events with model_variant and region to detect regional capacity issues vs model-specific problems.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: route-grace-window-service v0.1.0 promoted to staging at 2026-03-20T10:12:43Z :rocket:

Ryan: small nit — interaction with rate limit headers. If a request is queued, do we send back the immediate rate-limit headers or defer them until we actually process? clients rely on headers for local retry/backoff.

Maria: plan: return 102 Processing with `Retry-After` while queued (short ttl) so clients see they're in-flight. once processed, normal rate headers. any objections?

Sophia: 102 Processing is fine, but we need clear docs and a snippet for SDKs to show how to handle 102 vs 429. add to Console help and SDK changelogs.

Ashwin: and for telemetry, annotate traces with queued=true/false so we can trace tail-latency spikes.

Zara: deployment strategy: start as opt-in for a small % of tenants (canary) for 48h, then expand to 10% for a week, measure grace_success_rate and cost delta. if success_rate > 95% and cost delta < 5% roll to 100%.

Maria: agree. I'll draft the rollout checklist. action items:
- Maria: write RFC with config knobs and safety caps (due EOD)
- Ashwin: prototype detector & telemetry events (PR to observability)
- Ryan: quota-safe queued token calc + SDK guidance (PR)
- Sophia: Console mockups + help copy
- Zara: coordinate canary list and legal signoff for enterprise override

Sophia: ping me when you have mockups, I'll slot into next design review. :+1:

Ashwin: I'll add the reason codes and tracing annotations to the proto we use for routing events.

Maria: thanks all. one more: add a small CLI tool for operators to force-enter/exit grace for a route during incidents. helps debugging.

Ryan: tiny security note — queued requests live in memory; for Private deployments we must respect data residency and ensure queued payloads are not logged anywhere. add checklist item.

Zara: noted. I'll add compliance checkbox.

deploy-bot: NOTE: staging deploy succeeded. monitor dashboards at https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/route-grace (staging)

Maria: that's it for now. will share RFC link when ready. :seedling:
